title: A High-Yield Streptomyces Transcription-Translation Toolkit for Synthetic Biology and Natural Product Applications
protocol: Prepare 1 L of sterile GYM liquid medium in a 2 L baffled flask.
Prepare 50 mL of sterile GYM liquid medium in a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Prepare 100 mL of 1 M HEPES-KOH pH 7.5 solution.
Prepare 100 mL of 1 M MgCl2 solution.
Prepare 500 mL of 4 M NH4Cl solution.
Pre-warm the sterile GYM liquid medium to 28 °C for 30 min.
Inoculate a single colony from a GYM agar plate into prewarmed GYM liquid medium.
Incubate at 28 °C, 200 rpm for 16 h (overnight pre-culture).
Pre-warm 50 mL of sterile GYM liquid medium to 28 °C for 30 min.
Transfer 1 mL of overnight pre-culture into prewarmed GYM liquid medium.
Incubate at 28 °C, 200 rpm for 8 h (daytime pre-culture).
Check the OD600 in a spectrophotometer using a 1:10 dilution with sterile GYM medium.
Sub-culture 0.25 mL of daytime pre-culture into 1 L of liquid GYM medium in 2 L baffled flasks.
Shake overnight at 28 °C, 200 rpm for 14 h.
Record the OD600 of the main culture after the previous incubation period (14 h).
Dilute the overnight culture 1:10 with fresh GYM medium for OD600 measurement.
Increase shaking speed to 250-300 rpm if OD600 is less than 3.0 and grow until an OD600 of 3.0 is reached.
Transfer cultures to centrifugation containers and rapidly cool on wet ice for 30 min if OD600 is greater than 3.0.
Prepare 4 mL of fresh 1 M dithiothreitol (DTT), S30A, and S30B buffers while the cell culture cools on ice.
Pre-weigh an empty 50 mL centrifuge tube and pre-chill at -20 °C.
Add 2 mL of 1 M DTT to 1 L of S30A buffer on ice and mix well before use.
Centrifuge cells at 6,000 × g, 4 °C for 10 min after cooling the cultures.
Carefully discard the supernatant in a quick and single motion.
Add 500 mL of S30A buffer and resuspend the cells by shaking vigorously until clumps are homogeneously dispersed.
Centrifuge the cells at 6,000 × g, 4 °C for 6 min after resuspending the cells.
Add 2 mL of 1 M DTT to 1 L of S30B buffer on ice and mix well.
Add 500 mL of S30B buffer to the cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of S30B buffer and transfer to a pre-weighed, pre-chilled 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge cells at 6,000 × g, 4 °C, for 10 min, and carefully discard the supernatant.
Carefully aspirate the remaining S30B supernatant with a 100-200 μL pipette.
Weigh the wet cell pellet.
For every 1 g of wet cells, add 0.9 mL of S30B buffer to resuspend the cells.
Resuspend the cells using either a Pasteur pipette or vortex.
Centrifuge briefly (~10 s) at up to 500 × g to sediment the cells.
Rapidly thaw the 50 mL tube containing the pellet in lukewarm water if cells are frozen.
Transfer the thawed tube to wet ice and chill for 10 min.
Using a 1 mL pipette tip (cut off the end), transfer 1 mL of cell suspension into 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Place each microcentrifuge tube in a beaker of ice water using a plastic tube rack for sonication.
Clean the sonicator probe with 70% ethanol and double-distilled water.
Lower the sonicator tip into the cell suspension until it is ~1 cm below the liquid surface.
Input 20 kHz frequency into the sonicator.
Set the amplitude to 65% on the sonicator.
Configure a pulse ON time of 10 seconds.
Configure a pulse OFF time of 10 seconds.
Set total sonication time to 1 minute.
Run the sonication protocol.
Move the tube up/down and sideways during the first two resting cycles.
Record the energy input.
If necessary, repeat the sonication for an additional one or two 10 s cycles after inverting the tube 2-3 times.
Rapidly thaw a 50 mL tube containing the pellet in lukewarm water with shaking if cells are frozen.
Transfer the tube to wet ice as soon as the pellet has begun to defrost.
Chill for 10 minutes on wet ice.
Briefly spin the tube at 500 x g to sediment the cells.
Place the 50 mL tube in a beaker of ice water for sonication.
Clean the sonicator probe with 70% ethanol and ddH2O.
Lower the sonicator tip into the cell suspension until it is ~1 cm below the liquid surface.
Input 20 kHz frequency, 65% amplitude, 10 s pulse ON time, 10 s pulses OFF time, 1 min total sonication time per mL of wet cells (5 min in total) into the sonicator.
Run the sonication protocol while moving the tube up/down and sideways during the first two resting cycles.
Centrifuge the lysed cells at 16,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C to remove cell debris.
Transfer the supernatant into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes as 1 mL aliquots.
Incubate the 1.5 mL tubes containing the cell extracts at 30 °C for 60 min on a heat block or incubator without shaking.
Centrifuge the cell extracts at 16,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Pool the supernatants into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Mix the supernatant by inverting the tube five times until homogenous.
Keep the mixture on ice.
Invert gently to avoid the formation of air bubbles.
Dilute 10 µL of the cell extract 100-fold with S30B buffer.
Measure the total protein concentration using a Bradford assay with three technical repeats.
If the protein concentration is 20-25 mg/mL, transfer the cell extracts as 100 μL aliquots into new 1.5 mL tubes.
Flash-freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at -80 °C.

Purify the pTU1-A-SP44-mScarlet-I plasmid from a freshly transformed E. coli plasmid strain grown in 50 mL of LB culture with carbenicillin using an appropriate plasmid DNA purification kit as per manufacturer's instructions.
Elute the plasmid in 2 x 300 µL of nuclease-free water and combine the fractions.
Add 0.1 volumes (66 μL) of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2).
Add 0.7 volumes (462 μL) of isopropanol.
Incubate the DNA at -20 °C for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 2 mL of 70% (v/v) ethanol to the DNA pellet.
Invert the tube 3-4 times to resuspend the plasmid DNA pellet.
Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat steps 5.7-5.9 and remove all visible liquid.
Air-dry the DNA pellet for 10-30 min or dry for 5 min with a vacuum centrifuge.
Resuspend the dried pellet with 600 µL of nuclease-free ddH2O.
Measure the DNA concentration and purity using a spectrophotometer.
Prepare 50-100 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C.
Dilute the plasmid DNA stock to 80 nM; 168 ng/µL pTU1-A-SP44-mScarlet-I plasmid is equivalent to 80 nM.
Use the amino acid sampler kit following the manufacturer's instructions provided online.
Dilute the 20x amino acid stock solution using ddH2O to a final concentration of 6 mM (5 mM L-Leu).
Further dilute to 2.4 mM (2 mM L-Leu) within the 2.4x SMM solution.
Prepare the other components in the 2.4x SMM solution by following the recipe described in Table 3.
Thaw the cell extract, SMM (or MES) solution, and plasmid DNA on ice.
Pre-chill a 384-well plate at -20°C.
Set up TX-TL reactions with 25% volume of plasmid DNA, 33.33% volume of cell extract, and 41.67% volume of SMM solution.
Keep the reactions on ice to avoid start time bias.
Gently vortex the mixture for ~5 s at a low-speed setting to ensure homogeneity.
Transfer 10 μl aliquots into three wells of a 384-well plate as technical triplicates without introducing air bubbles.
Seal the plate with a transparent cover and spin at 400 × g for 5 s.
Incubate the reaction at 28°C either in an incubator or plate-reader without shaking.
